## Enhancements

- Support for polyform queries

- `Mercator`: Transform `Geometry` objects from Mercator projection to WGS-84 via `unproject()`
 
## Internal

- Removal of obsolete classes

This release supports Version 2.0 of the Geo-Object Library file format.

**Important:** GOL 2.0 is incompatible with GOL 1.0. To create GOLs from OSM data, use GOL Tool 2.0 ([download](https://www.geodesk.com/download) • [repo](https://github.com/clarisma/geodesk-gol)).

We've prepared a [Migration Guide](https://github.com/clarisma/geodesk/blob/main/doc/migrating.md) to ensure your upgrade goes smoothly.

## Breaking changes

- Requires GOLs created with [GOL Tool 2.0](https://github.com/clarism

## Enhancements

- Queries based on a feature's ID (but see [documentation](http://docs.geodesk.com/java/queries#querying-features-by-id) for important notes on performance)

## Bug fixes

- Fixed strict-mode Decimal parsing (#102)

With automatic updates on (macOS and Linux, from 0.1.5), this release installs by itself overnight, or straight away from **Settings, Updates**. Otherwise run the same command to update: your settings and your data stay as they are, and the database is brought up to date when it starts. See the [README](https://github.com/pental-io/report#readme) for a server with your own domain, installing by hand, and backups.

- **Updates, said and installed.** When a new release is out, administrators see it in **Settings, Updates**, with what it changes, and in a banner at the top of the page when there is something to do about it. On Linux and macOS the installer now offers to set up a small updater on the computer it runs on, and yes is its default: a new release then installs overnight, between 1am and 6am on that computer's clock, or straight away when you press **Update Now**. The updater copies the database to `backups/`
